programs.title: Memory of the World: When China Echoes Ep.5
programs.desc: Drawing on Chinese archives inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World—including oracle bones and Qing examination result lists—this series uses small artifacts to tell grand stories, preserving China's heritage for China, and for all humanity.

programs.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga & Choy Li Fut
programs.desc: In Foshan, kung fu is daily life. Kleber visits Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut masters, tries traditional massage and lion dance, explores lion head craftsmanship — Lingnan charm of kung fu rooted in local soil.

programs.title: Kungfu-wise: Taiji Quan
programs.desc: Kleber studies Taiji with master Chen Ziqiang in Chenjiagou. Gentle movements with combat power. He tries practical training, visits historic sites, and feels Taiji’s folk roots and local attachment.

programs.title: Human Carbon Footprint
programs.desc: How exactly does China drive green development and harmony with nature? Examples like smart mining at Heidaigou Opencast Coal Mine, cleaner fossil fuel use, and a thermal plant working alongside renewables offer part of the answer.

programs.title: Secrets of the Flaming Mountains Ep.1
programs.desc: In 908, a Central Asian expedition to the Flaming Mountains in Xinjiang, China, made a startling discovery—mummified remains buried in the Astana Cemetery, unlocking a mystery over a thousand years old. Meanwhile, a revered Buddhist monk and a Central Asian king forged a life-and-death bond—one of the most extraordinary friendships in Buddhist history. But what really happened? And what would eventually lead to the fall of the once-thriving Gaochang Kingdom.
